subject: Intermittent TLS handshake failures during private peering — SYN race suspected
messages:
From: Beth Chambers <beth@dovetail.health>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@dovetail.health
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent TLS failures from clients to private-hosted endpoints

Markus, Vanessa —

We started seeing a spike of customer errors this morning where HTTPS connections to our private-hosted endpoints (over our cross-connect into Redwood private VPC) fail during the TLS handshake. The symptom on our side is: client SYN -> server SYN-ACK observed, then our client retransmits SYN and the handshake never completes for ~0.5-2s before the app retries. ~2.3% of requests in the window 08:55-09:15 PST failed.

We captured a short pcap from our edge (attached) — you'll see duplicate SYNs from the same client src-port arriving at different Redwood egress IPs, and SYN-ACKs coming back but not matching the conn state we see locally. We suspect some form of asymmetric handling or ephemeral port mapping getting lost across your middlebox.

Environment: we connect via a private dedicated VLAN (Equinix colocation), BGP session with your edge routers; our border devices run IOS-XE. We've not made any changes on our side since yesterday.

Attachments: dovetail_tls_failures_20261107.pcap, short trace of failing request IDs.

Can you triage? This is impacting a handful of production customers. We can open a maintenance window if a temporary routing change is needed.

Thanks,
Beth Chambers
Network Reliability Lead
Dovetail Health

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Beth Chambers <beth@dovetail.health>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures from clients to private-hosted endpoints

Thanks Beth — sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as an urgent triage. Initial asks:

1) Can you confirm the exact client IPs and timestamps (we only need 3-5 examples) so we can cross-check on our egresses?
2) Can you run tcpdump on your ingress facing the cross-connect: tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/edge-syn.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (syn) != 0' for 5 mins and share?
3) We'll need the BGP adjacency state around the events (show ip bgp neighbors and counters).

Immediate plan on our side: I am pinging network on-call (Connor) and infra (Karthik) to collect: interface counters, ECMP hash stability, NAT session summaries, and any load‑balancer stickiness changes. My suspicion from the pcap is a SYN duplication/race where SYNs take different egress paths and the SYN-ACKs end up hitting a device without the forward state (either due to SNAT not being preserved across ECMP or a conntrack race).

If confirmed, a short mitigation is to pin flows at our egress for Dovetail prefixes (policy route for your /24s) to enforce symmetric NAT during the window. We can schedule that for a 30-min window as soon as you provide a window.

I've attached an internal runbook link we will follow. I'll update after initial collectors return.

—Markus
Head of Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Beth Chambers <beth@dovetail.health>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures from clients to private-hosted endpoints

Quick status from edge: I pulled the pcap — there are repeated SYNs from the same tuple showing up on two different egress neighbors within ~30ms of each other. On our edge routers I'm seeing:

- BGP route flaps for one of the intermediate transit hops at 08:58:13 and 09:02:47 (matching your window).
- ECMP hashing is changing due to interface state changes (we see L2 neighbor flaps).
- Netfilter conntrack entries show short-lived SYN entries that expire before the SYN-ACK completes when the SYN/ACK returns via a different path.

I also see occasional ICMP frag-needed messages on the path but the devices are configured to rate-limit those; unsure if it contributed.

Proposed immediate actions (safe, reversible):
- Apply a temporary per-prefix policy route for Dovetail /24s that pins to a single egress pair (no ECMP) for 30 minutes.
- Turn on per-flow hashing on the affected egress if available to reduce multi-path duplication.

Connor, Karthik — can you prepare the config diff? Beth — would you be able to accept a 30-min window starting 11:30 PST?

V.| Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, beth@dovetail.health
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures from clients to private-hosted endpoints

I ran counters and dug into conntrack:

- show interfaces counters: small RX errors on egress1 at 08:58:13 correlated with the upstream flap.
- show ip route and bgp summary: neighbor 198.51.100.14 showed a 1xx flaps count in the last hour.
- conntrack -L | grep SYN shows pockets of SYN entries created and expired (timeout ~30s) with no established entry when SYN-ACKs returned on the alternate path.

I prepared a config diff to implement Vanessa's temporary policy (attached: proposed-temporary-policy.diff). The change pins your prefixes to egress pair A via policy-based routing and sets a short hold-time to revert after 30 mins. I tested the change in staging and saw the dup-SYN condition disappear in a controlled load test.

Planned maintenance: 11:30–12:00 PST today. During that window we'll:
- Apply PBR pin for Dovetail /24s.
- Monitor tcpdump counters and conntrack for your sample client IPs.
- If successful, schedule a longer-term fix (sticky hashing or hardware replacement).

Karthik — if you can stand by for any gateway NAT parameter tweaks in-case we still see asymmetry.

Connor O'Brien
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Beth Chambers <beth@dovetail.health>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures from clients to private-hosted endpoints

11:30–12:00 PST works for us. We will keep application teams on standby and provide three client IPs and three timestamps (attached in the Drive link). We have also attached the full pcap for your correlation.

A couple of asks:
- Please capture tcpdump on both egress devices and include timestamps; that will help us confirm the path consistency.
- If this is a config change on Redwood side that might trigger retries or short connection resets, please provide a brief rollback procedure.

Also asking about SLA impact — can we discuss provisional credits if the root cause is on Redwood side? We can circle back on commercial after we stabilize.

Thanks — Beth

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Beth Chambers <beth@dovetail.health>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures from clients to private-hosted endpoints

Post-mitigation summary and next steps:

Outcome from 11:30–12:00 PST window:
- Applied temporary PBR pin for Dovetail prefixes at 11:31 PST; monitored for 30 minutes.
- Client failure rate dropped from ~2.3% to 0.2% in the sample window.
- Collected tcpdumps on both sides and conntrack logs; correlated to show that duplicate SYNs ceased when flows were pinned to a single egress.

Root cause hypothesis: transient L2 neighbor instability at the colo causing ECMP path churn, which in turn produced out-of-order SYN arrivals across egress nodes. The combination of short-lived conntrack entries and asymmetric return paths led to SYN state being lost on the return path occasionally, causing TLS handshake failures. There is a secondary observation of ICMP frag-needed suppression on the path (we will include MTU in the long-term follow-up).

Action items (owners and timeline):
- Connor: open a hardware ticket with the colo provider for the flapping transit hop (done, TKT-209334). Provide status in 24h.
- Karthik: schedule a config CR to enable per-flow sticky hashing on affected egresses (CR# 20261108-03). Target: 2026-11-12.
- Vanessa: prepare postmortem with packet timelines and add MTU validation steps to the private-deploy checklist. Due: 2026-11-10.
- Markus: follow up with Dovetail on SLA discussion and compile traces to support any credits request.

Beth — thanks for the fast collaboration and providing pcaps. We'll keep this thread for follow-ups and postmortem when completed. If anything regresses please reopen immediately and we'll escalate to on-call leadership.

Best,
Markus
Head of Network Reliability, Redwood Inference
